Consult Summary:
- Acute diarrheal illness with abdominal pain for ~3 days; patient remains hydrated and tolerating fluids; dietary management and home care discussed.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 3-day history of diarrhea with abdominal pain; 4–5 bowel movements per day; stool consistency variable (water/loose); one episode of vomiting; no blood or mucus reported; mild fever possible but not concerning; appetite reduced.
- Onset/progression: Symptoms began ~3 days ago and have persisted; no recent travel or questionable foods reported.
- Past medical history: Asthma (inhaler used; name reported by patient as “Lexapro”; dose/route/frequency not documented). Family history: father had hypertension; father died of bowel cancer at 62.
- Allergies: None.
- Medications: Lexapro (asthma inhaler? name provided by patient); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Not provided.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Impression:
- Acute gastroenteritis/diarrhea without dehydration at present; no red flags identified on history (no blood in stool; able to drink).

Plan:
- Diet and hydration:
  - Soft diet during diarrhea; avoid dairy, fish, meat, and eggs while symptomatic.
  - Suggested foods: crackers, toast, jam; then gradually introduce boiled vegetables and mash; after ~48 hours with no diarrhea, reintroduce meat.
  - Consider probiotic yogurt to support gut flora.
  - Ensure adequate fluids; consider over-the-counter Dioralyte to replenish salts and fluids.
- Activity/monitoring:
  - If diarrhea worsens to 6–8 stools per day, increased dehydration risk; may require hospital assessment.
  - If diarrhea persists beyond 1 week or if there is blood in stool, obtain a stool sample.
- Medications/antibiotics:
  - No antibiotics prescribed at this time.
- Follow-up and resources:
  - All information recorded in patient app; follow notes for details.
  - Contact provider if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.
